questions.text: Which feature of OOP hides the internal details of an object and exposes only what is needed?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation binds data and methods together and hides the data behind access control.

questions.text: A class in Java is
options: a blueprint from which objects are created
a method that returns an object
questions.explanation: A class defines the fields and methods; objects are created from it with new.

questions.text: Which keyword creates a new object in Java?
questions.explanation: new allocates memory for an object and calls its constructor.

questions.text: Java source code is compiled into
options: bytecode that runs on the JVM
questions.explanation: javac produces .class files of bytecode, which the Java Virtual Machine runs on any platform.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a primitive type in Java?
questions.explanation: String is a class in java.lang; the eight primitives are byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean.

questions.text: What is the size of an int in Java?
questions.explanation: Java fixes int at 32 bits on every platform.

questions.text: What is the default value of a boolean field of a class?
questions.explanation: Fields of a class get default values; a boolean field defaults to false.

questions.text: Which statement about constructors is true?
options: A constructor must have a return type
A constructor has the same name as its class and no return type
A class can have only one constructor
questions.explanation: A constructor is named after the class, has no return type, and can be overloaded; it is not inherited.

questions.text: The keyword 'this' refers to
questions.explanation: this is a reference to the object on which the method or constructor was called.

questions.text: Which access modifier makes a member visible only inside its own class?
questions.explanation: private members are accessible only within the declaring class.

questions.text: A member with no access modifier (default) is visible
questions.explanation: Default (package-private) access allows any class in the same package.

questions.text: A static method
options: needs an object to be called
belongs to the class and can be called without an object
questions.explanation: Static members belong to the class itself, so they are called as ClassName.method().

questions.text: Which keyword is used to inherit from a class in Java?
questions.explanation: class B extends A makes B a subclass of A.

questions.text: Java does not support multiple inheritance of classes. Which construct gives a form of multiple inheritance?
questions.explanation: A class can implement many interfaces, though it extends only one class.

questions.text: The keyword 'super' is used to
options: call a method of the same class
refer to the immediate parent class's members or constructor
questions.explanation: super() calls the parent constructor and super.method() calls the parent's version.

questions.text: Method overloading means
options: same name, different parameter lists in one class
same signature in parent and child classes
questions.explanation: Overloaded methods share a name but differ in the number or types of parameters; it is resolved at compile time.

questions.text: Method overriding is an example of
questions.explanation: Which overridden method runs is decided at run time by the actual object (dynamic method dispatch).

questions.text: A final method
questions.explanation: final on a method prevents subclasses from overriding it; final on a class prevents inheritance.

questions.text: An abstract class
options: cannot be instantiated and may have abstract methods
questions.explanation: An abstract class can have both abstract and concrete methods and constructors, but no objects of it can be created.

questions.text: Since Java 8, an interface can contain
questions.explanation: Java 8 added default and static methods to interfaces; their fields are implicitly public static final.

questions.text: Fields declared in an interface are implicitly
questions.explanation: Interface fields are constants: public, static and final.

questions.text: Which package is imported automatically into every Java program?
questions.explanation: java.lang (String, Math, Object, System and others) is always available without import.

questions.text: Which is the root class of every class in Java?
questions.explanation: Every class directly or indirectly extends java.lang.Object.

questions.text: What does the following print? String s1 = "java"; String s2 = new String("java"); System.out.println(s1 == s2);
questions.explanation: == compares references; new String creates a different object, so it prints false. equals() would compare content.

questions.text: Strings in Java are
questions.explanation: A String object cannot change; operations like concat return a new String. StringBuilder is the mutable alternative.

questions.text: Which class should be used to build a string in a loop efficiently in a single thread?
questions.explanation: StringBuilder is mutable and not synchronized, so it is the fastest for single-threaded building.

questions.text: Which block always runs, whether or not an exception occurs?
questions.explanation: finally runs after try and catch, used to release resources.

questions.text: Which of these is a checked exception?
questions.explanation: IOException must be caught or declared; the others are unchecked RuntimeExceptions.

questions.text: The 'throws' keyword is used to
options: declare that a method may throw exceptions
questions.explanation: throws in a method signature declares the checked exceptions it may pass to the caller; throw raises one.

questions.text: What happens with: int[] a = new int[3]; a[3] = 5;
questions.explanation: Valid indexes are 0 to 2, so index 3 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at run time.

questions.text: Which is the superclass of all exceptions and errors?
questions.explanation: Throwable is the root; Exception and Error both extend it.

questions.text: A custom checked exception is created by
questions.explanation: Extending Exception (but not RuntimeException) makes a checked exception.

questions.text: Which method starts a new thread of execution?
questions.explanation: start() creates the new thread, which then calls run(); calling run() directly runs on the current thread.

questions.text: A thread can be created in Java by
questions.explanation: The two classic ways are subclassing Thread and passing a Runnable to a Thread.

questions.text: The 'synchronized' keyword is used to
options: let only one thread at a time execute a block on the same lock
questions.explanation: synchronized makes threads acquire an object's monitor, preventing race conditions.

questions.text: Which method makes the current thread wait until another thread finishes?
questions.explanation: t.join() blocks until thread t has finished.

questions.text: wait(), notify() and notifyAll() are methods of
questions.explanation: They are defined in java.lang.Object and must be called while holding the object's lock.

questions.text: Which thread state is entered after calling sleep(1000)?
questions.explanation: A thread sleeping for a set time is in TIMED_WAITING until the time passes.

questions.text: Which collection does NOT allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: A Set holds each element once; Lists allow duplicates.

questions.text: Which Map implementation keeps its keys sorted?
questions.explanation: TreeMap is a red-black tree that keeps keys in their natural or a given order.

questions.text: ArrayList gives fast
questions.explanation: ArrayList is backed by an array, so get(i) is O(1); inserting at the front shifts every element.

questions.text: Which interface must a class implement to be sorted by Collections.sort() using its natural order?
questions.explanation: Comparable's compareTo defines the natural order; a Comparator is a separate ordering object.

questions.text: Which stream class reads characters from a file?
questions.explanation: Reader classes like FileReader handle characters; InputStream classes handle bytes.

questions.text: What is the output of: System.out.println(10 / 4 + 10 % 4);
questions.explanation: 10 / 4 is integer division = 2, and 10 % 4 = 2, so 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.text: Which statement about garbage collection is true?
options: System.gc() frees memory immediately and always
An object becomes eligible when no live reference points to it
Programmers must free memory with delete
Garbage collection runs only when the program ends
questions.explanation: The JVM reclaims objects that are no longer reachable; System.gc() is only a request.
